title: Learnware Specification via Dual Alignment
reviewed_version: Published ICML 2025 proceedings, PMLR 267; 17-page staged PDF
summary: Two demonstrated defects affect the theoretical support for the dual-alignment objective: an attained positive alignment optimum and an invalid MMD deviation inequality.
limitations: No author-code execution or empirical reproduction.
Separate OpenReview supplements unavailable in source manifest.
No released repository identified in acquired sources.
No later-version or global erratum search.
Proposition 4.3 external theorem not independently reconstructed.

problems.source_claim: Proposition 4.5 asserts simultaneous performance and barycenter alignment at an optimized specification.
problems.location: PDF p.5 Proposition 4.5, Eq.(8); Appendix C pp.14-17, Eq.(45)
assumptions: D has 50 copies each of +/-e1; indexed training samples allow repetitions
Gaussian ReLU embedding; classifier same hidden architecture with one-logit softmax
problems.check: L_MMD >= 1/8 + (||z||-1/2)^2/2; equality at +/-e1/2. The discriminative term is constant sqrt(alpha).
problems.result: Full global minimum exists but distribution loss is 1/8, so exact simultaneous alignment fails.
problems.counterevidence: Approximate improvement is not refuted. A new exact-representability hypothesis would change the theorem; no such hypothesis appears. Empirical Figure 3 is not a universal proof.
problems.core_dependency: The minimizer guarantee justifies the central objective and is explicitly used by Proposition 4.6.

correction.reason: A general residual/convergence theorem has not been established.

problems.source_claim: Equation (24) upper-bounds an absolute supremum deviation by a supremum of signed deviations; Eq.(7) uses empirical Rademacher complexities.
problems.location: PDF p.13 Eq.(24), pp.13-14 Eqs.(25)-(28), p.5 Proposition 4.4 Eq.(7)
assumptions: Singleton f(x)=ReLU(x), bounded inputs and weight norm 1
For Eq.(24), p=Bernoulli(3/4), q=Bernoulli(1/4), D={1}, R={0}; independent event probability 9/16
For literal Eq.(7), p=q=Bernoulli(1/2), n=100,m=1, delta=1/4
problems.check: Eq.(24) would require 0.5 <= -0.5. Singleton empirical complexities are zero, while the squared sample-mean gap is positive with probability 1-2^-100 under p=q.
problems.result: Signed-deviation step invalid. Literal complexity formulation of Eq.(7) also fails.
problems.counterevidence: Interpreting the complexity symbols as positive norm upper bounds avoids the zero-complexity example but does not repair Eq.(24) or justify the objective/sampling transition.
problems.core_dependency: Proposition 4.4 is the theoretical distribution-alignment bound used directly to justify DALI.

correction.statement: Absolute difference of finite suprema <= supremum of absolute differences; no full concentration theorem repaired.
